messages:
nina: Heads-up: ran into an auth nightmare while iterating on the new sample-app. Local .env has REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY, my shell has REDWOOD_ORG_KEY, and the Node SDK ended up sending both. Backend rejects and SDK aborts the retry loop. Anyone want to weigh in on precedence and a UX for rotation?

omar: Yikes. Quick question: are both headers present or does the SDK pick one then fallback?

nina: Both. Example from proxy logs:

```
POST /v1/chat/stream
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer org_live_z23",
  "X-Redwood-Project-Key": "proj_live_kjl",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
Response: 401 {"error":"conflicting_auth","detail":"multiple tokens present"}
```

ravi: We intentionally allowed legacy project header for backward compatibility, but sending two tokens should never happen. We need: 1) a consistent cross-SDK precedence, 2) dev-time diagnostics, and 3) safer stream recovery on mid-stream 401 during rotation.

nina: For diagnostics, a runtime warning at startup when >1 auth source detected would have saved me 10-15 min. Also would be nice if the SDK printed which source won.

omar: Agreed. Proposal: precedence order = explicit param > CLI flag > REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY env > REDWOOD_ORG_KEY env > netrc > legacy file. Rationale: explicit overrides are obvious; project env should outrank org env so local devs can scope to project easily. But open to debate.

ravi: I'd flip project/org in precedence: org env should outrank project env for CI consistency. Otherwise CI injecting ORG can be silently trumped by a checked-in PROJECT .env. That caused flakes in our CI last week.

nina: Good point. Maybe require explicit opt-in to let project env override org env (e.g., REDWOOD_ALLOW_PROJECT_OVERRIDE=true). Default: org wins in shared environments; project env is for local dev when not present in shell.

omar: Nice compromise. Also add a CLI flag `--auth-source` to force which token to use; useful for debugging and CI.

ravi: About stream recovery: when a 401 occurs mid-stream, SDK should not immediately close the user-level stream. Instead: run onAuthRefresh hook (async) to attempt a token swap, then retry the failed frame(s). If refresh succeeds, resume transparent to the caller; if it fails, then surface an error and close. The hook should be pluggable per-SDK.

nina: Also add a rate-limited dev warning when multiple sources seen. Rate-limit to once per minute and include a link to docs. Example message: `WARN devex auth: multiple auth sources detected; using ORG env. Run with --auth-source to override. See https://redwood.dev/auth-precedence`

omar: For rotation we discovered netrc-cached tokens can be stale and cause intermittent 403s after nightly rotation. On 403/401 from token marked as cache/netrc, invalidate that cache entry and re-resolve sources once before failing. That handles rotated tokens gracefully.

ravi: Also add telemetry (dev-only) header X-Auth-Resolution: <source> so ops can triage in staging without exposing secrets. Only include in non-prod builds.

kg-bot: note: add SDK conformance test matrix across node/python/rust to verify precedence + streaming 401 behavior. Ticket: DEVEX-AuthParity-472.

infra-ci: build: sample-app e2e (1781234000) failed during auth smoke tests.

nina: I'll open a small PR for the sample-app Dockerfile to stop copying .env and include a .env.example. I'll also add a tiny repro script and the logs.

omar: I'll draft the SDK RFC with the precedence rules and the onAuthRefresh hook spec. Will include sample code for Node and Python.

ravi: Friendly reminder: document the REDWOOD_ALLOW_PROJECT_OVERRIDE flag and default behavior in the onboarding guide. Also add a troubleshooting snippet for "conflicting_auth" errors in the SDK errors page.

nina: Thanks all  I'll include the rate-limit and the --auth-source flag in the PR. Happy to pair on the conformance tests.
